# Scale & Physical AI Principles {.unnumbered}

Part IV scales agentic systems to distributed multi-agent fleets, datacenter economics, and physical embodiment. It establishes the Actor model for multi-agent fleets, telemetry via OpenTelemetry GenAI standards, Trajectory Goodput optimization, and the critical bridge to continuous, real-time cyber-physical systems in Volume IV.

::: {#pri-vol3-stochastic-actors .callout-principle title="Asynchronous Stochastic Actor Concurrency"}

**Invariant**: Multi-agent collaboration must be engineered as asynchronous actors with isolated state and explicit message channels, strictly bounded by the Coordination Tax.

**Implication**: Language models sharing base distributions exhibit correlated failures; peer-to-peer debate amplifies hallucinations rather than eliminating them.

:::

::: {#pri-vol3-causal-lineage .callout-principle title="Causal Lineage and Distributional Benchmarking"}

**Invariant**: Stochastic agent systems cannot be evaluated by static scalar benchmarks; evaluation requires interactive environment gyms measuring task completion distributions and causal span telemetry.

**Implication**: Replay debugging requires capturing non-deterministic PRNG seeds and mocking tool I/O to achieve bit-exact offline trajectory reproduction.

:::

::: {#pri-vol3-improvement-ladder .callout-principle title="The Post-Training Improvement Ladder"}

**Invariant**: Systems optimization follows an economic hierarchy: exhaust runtime scaffolding (prompts, contexts, tools, verifiers) before amortizing search into compile-time weights via RLVR.

**Implication**: Raw token throughput is a vanity metric; agent clusters must be optimized for Trajectory Goodput (verified task outcomes per dollar per GPU-hour).

:::

::: {#pri-vol3-causal-realtime .callout-principle title="The Causal Real-Time Boundary"}

**Invariant**: When actions transition from discrete digital APIs to continuous physical plants, asynchronous token generation must interface with synchronous, hard real-time sensorimotor loops via deterministic safety shields.

**Implication**: In physical systems, time flows relentlessly (t > 0); deliberative planners must be decoupled from high-frequency motor loops mediated by Control Barrier Functions.

:::
